items.q: Antidepressant therapeutic onset and continuation after first depressive episode remission are typically what?
o: 2 to 6 weeks onset; continue 6 to 12 months after remission
Three months onset; stop in 2 weeks
items.exp: Early review at 2 to 4 weeks judges tolerability and trajectory, full effect by 6 weeks at adequate dose, continuation 6 to 12 months (longer recurrent) prevents relapse, then gradual taper.
r: Incorrect. Onset lags and early stop relapses.
Incorrect. Neither instant nor universally lifelong.
items.kp: Slow on, stay months, taper slow.

items.q: Electric shock sensations, dizziness and irritability three days after stopping paroxetine abruptly indicate what?
items.exp: Short half life agents (paroxetine, venlafaxine) cause discontinuation symptoms within days (FINISH pattern) resolving on reinstatement and slower taper, unlike relapse emerging weeks later with original symptoms.
r: Incorrect. Relapse takes weeks and lacks shocks.
Incorrect. No serotonergic excess or clonus.
items.kp: Zap sensations after abrupt stop equals discontinuation.

items.q: Which antidepressant is most dangerous in overdose and avoided where suicide risk high?
items.exp: Tricyclics block cardiac sodium channels causing arrhythmia, seizures and death in small multiples of daily dose, so safer SSRIs are chosen in risky patients and quantities limited.
r: Incorrect. SSRIs relatively safe in overdose.
items.kp: Tricyclic bottle can be a lethal weapon.

items.q: Agitation, fever, diarrhoea, tremor and inducible clonus after adding tramadol to SSRI indicates what and first action?
o: Serotonin syndrome; stop serotonergic agents, benzodiazepine and supportive cooling
items.exp: Serotonergic stacking produces hyperactive neuromuscular signs distinct from NMS; cessation, sedation, fluids and temperature control with cyproheptadine for moderate severe cases in monitored settings treats it.
r: Incorrect. Exposure and clonus say serotonin.
Correct. Stop serotonergics and sedate cool.
Incorrect. Sepsis may mimic but drug timing directs action.
items.kp: Clonus after tramadol plus SSRI: stop both.

items.q: Required washout between stopping fluoxetine and starting an MAOI is about what and why?
o: Five weeks; long lived norfluoxetine metabolite
items.exp: Norfluoxetine persists weeks, so MAOI within five weeks risks serotonin syndrome; most other SSRI to MAOI gaps are about two weeks per specific guidance.

items.q: Lithium level sampling standard timing is what?
o: About 12 hours after last dose at steady state
items.exp: Twelve hour standardised levels make results comparable for narrow index dosing, checked after dose changes (about a week steady state) and during illness, dehydration or interacting drug starts.
r: Correct. Twelve hour post dose level.
Incorrect. Timing anchored to dose matters.
items.kp: Twelve hours after pill, lithium tells truth.

items.q: Which co prescriptions commonly precipitate lithium toxicity by reducing clearance?
o: NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors and thiazides (plus dehydration)
items.exp: Renal prostaglandin or sodium handling changes raise lithium reabsorption; sick day rules pause lithium during vomiting, diarrhoea or poor intake with urgent level and renal checks.
r: Correct. NSAID, ACE inhibitor, thiazide triad.
items.kp: Painkillers, pressure pills and water pills poison lithium.

items.q: Long term lithium monitoring must include which organ systems besides levels?
items.exp: Hypothyroidism, hyperparathyroidism hypercalcaemia and renal impairment (including nephrogenic diabetes insipidus polyuria) accrue over years, needing scheduled TFT, calcium and eGFR with urine symptoms review.
r: Incorrect. Eye exams not lithium schedule core.

items.q: Valproate in a 19 year old woman requires what mandatory safeguard?
o: Pregnancy prevention programme: teratogenicity counselling, contraception and annual specialist review per regulations
items.exp: Valproate causes neural tube defects and neurodevelopmental harm with high absolute risks, so regulators require documented counselling, effective contraception and specialist annual acknowledgement in women of childbearing potential, preferring alternatives.
r: Incorrect. Folate does not neutralise risk.
Incorrect. First trimester organogenesis is critical.
items.kp: Valproate plus possible pregnancy needs programme lock.

items.q: Lamotrigine titration must be slow primarily to prevent what, and valproate does what to its level?
o: Stevens Johnson syndrome; valproate inhibits metabolism doubling levels (halve dose)
items.exp: Rapid escalation risks serious rash including Stevens Johnson, so slow schedules with valproate co therapy halved (glucuronidation inhibition) and stopped urgently for concerning rash with systemic features.
r: Correct. Rash prevention; valproate doubles lamotrigine.
Incorrect. Blood dyscrasia is carbamazepine or clozapine.
items.kp: Slow lamotrigine, half with valproate, watch skin.
